newsitem.title: UK: European bourses fall on EMU,election worries.
newsitem.headline: European bourses fall on EMU,election worries.

text.p: European bourses fell on Tuesday despite a spectacular comeback on Wall Street overnight, with London already suffering pre-election jitters and continental markets fretting over EMU.

The dollar continued easing against yen and mark, despite comments from a senior Bundesbanker that EMU (European economic and monetary union) should be delayed if Germany could not meet the entry criteria.
On the share markets, Wall Street had little influence even though the Dow Jones Industrial Average recovered from an early 80 point loss on Monday to close up 20.02, at 6,955.48.

Investors in Europe, where markets tumbled on Monday, had their own worries, not to mention fears that the U.S. central bank might raise interest rates when its Federal Open Market Committee meets on March 25.

London, which shrugged off Prime Minister John Major's announcement of a May 1 general election on Monday, suddenly started worrying about a six-week campaign and the prospect of a change in government. By noon the FTSE-100 index was down 20.3 points at 4,353.0.
"The market is a bit fraught," said the head of equity trading at one brokerage. "It is in a bit of disarray, there is uncertainty for the next six weeks."
The election date came as no surprise to markets, but with the opposition far ahead in opinion polls, traders began to contemplate life under a Labour government.
Financial markets are traditionally hostile to Labour, but leader Tony Blair has dragged the party towards the centre and made efforts to woo the business community.
Blair has not won over the entire financial community with his promises of no return to traditional Labour policies of "tax and spend".

"It is an incredible lead Labour has got," said a senior trader at a U.S. securities house. "People will start to think about the amount of interference that is going to take place under a Labour government."

The trader also attributed the weak start to the fact that U.S. bonds had failed to follow the Dow rally. "Bonds are still deteriorating and that is still the key as far as we are concerned," he said.

Other European equity markets were likewise weak. In Paris the CAC-40 index was 12.01 lower at 2,576.37 after tumbling two percent on Monday, while in Germany the DAX shed almost one percent or 32.19 points to 3,318.80.

German shares suffered from growing concerns that Bonn might fail to cut its budget deficit to three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) this year, a target for EMU membership, forcing a delay in the whole project's scheduled start in January 1999.

Bundesbank council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher was quoted on Tuesday as doubting that Germany could meet convergency targets and the start of EMU could have to be delayed. "If Germany can't meet EMU targets the markets are going to fall sharply," one senior trader said.
Frankfurt also buzzed about a possible bid for steel giant Thyssen AG by Hoesch-Krupp . Shares in both were suspended by the German stock exchange.
Thyssen said in a statement late on Monday that Krupp planned a hostile takeover and that it would use "all appropriate measures" to ward off its rival.
Following the suspensions, Thyssen shares were changing hands in unofficial trade at around 395 marks each, well above the 346.80 in bourse trade on Monday.
On foreign exchange markets, the dollar edged below 1.69 marks and 123 yen despite the Kuehbacher comments.

The yen was firm after the announcement of a Japanese government scheme to improve land sales plus comments from a Bank of Japan (BOJ) official which dealers interpreted as a check on falling long-term interest rates.

But some were cautious. "The market may be reading too much into the BOJ comments and the land liquidity plans. The market is getting increasingly nervous into the financial year-end," said a German bank dealer.
By noon, the dollar had slipped to 1.6870 marks from 1.6901 in European trading late on Monday, while it had eased to 122.81 yen from 123.63.
CURRENCIES AT 1200 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6870 marks and 122.81 yen, compared with Monday's late European levels of 1.6901 marks and 123.63 yen.
STOCK MARKETS at 1200 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 20.3 points at 4,353.0.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 12.01 points at 2,576.37.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was 32.19 points lower (0.96 percent) at 3,318.80.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $347.40 an ounce in the morning, compared with $350.25 at the close on Monday. Silver was at $5.21, compared with $5.23.
